blogs.title: Unpacking RLHF: Why Fine‑Tuning LLMs With Human Feedback Is Hard
blogs.description: Learn how large language models are initially trained in an unsupervised way, and why alignment requires extra steps—collecting relative quality labels, fitting reward models via the Bradley‑Terry formula, then tackling hard reinforcement‑learning pipelines that demand careful hyperparameter tuning and costly sampling.

blogs.title: Direct Preference Optimization Made Simple
blogs.description: Discover Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), a new algorithm that removes both the explicit reward model and the reinforcement‑learning loop, instead training directly from human preference pairs with an ordinary binary cross‑entropy loss.

blogs.title: Behind the Scenes of DPO
blogs.description: Dive into the math that makes DPO work—the trick of expressing any Bayesian‑optimal reward as “reward = β·log(p / p_ref)”—so we can translate preference statistics straight into an optimal policy without estimating partition functions.

blogs.title: DPO vs PPO—Why Simple Is Stronger
blogs.description: See how experiments across sentiment control, summarization and single‑turn dialogue show DPO achieves equal or better win rates than PPO‑based RLHF while requiring far less training time and almost no hyperparameter tinkering.

blogs.title: What This Means for Building Aligned LLMs
blogs.description: Explore how removing reinforcement learning simplifies engineering pipelines, lowers barriers to creating custom aligned models up to multi‑billion parameters—and what questions remain about scaling effects and safety beyond current benchmarks.
